RouteStick.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    remaining_path
        When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, decode the entire demonstration in two stages. First identify the starting target and the chronological sequence of arrivals at adjacent target identities, using highlight transitions together with wrist approach. Count an arrival even if the exact resting instant is absent from the sampled frames and the wrist has already begun departing in the next frame. A temporary double highlight belongs to one arrival transition, not an extra traversal; small coordinate fluctuations do not create new target identities. Every return to a previously visited target counts again. Split at every arrival before classifying arcs, preserving every repeated traversal and reversal rather than merging repeated visits into a broad excursion. Build a temporary chronological traversal ledger with one row per adjacent-target arrival: departure and arrival target identities, departure and arrival wrist resting positions, and that traversal's intermediate wrist samples. A delayed highlight may confirm an arrival after the wrist has begun departing again; assign samples by the wrist's arrival boundary, not the later highlight time, so the next departure's samples belong to the next traversal. The ledger is only a decoding aid, not persistent memory. Second classify each resulting traversal independently, checking every segment including the final one. For each segment, calculate its own destination target x minus departure target x and compare only that segment's intermediate wrist samples with its own resting-endpoint baseline. Never inherit an arc label from the preceding segment, infer the arc from direction alone, or assume that a reversal uses the opposite image arc. Determine direction from destination target x minus departure target x, not from local wrist motion during the arc. Determine the arc from intermediate wrist positions relative to the line joining the departure and arrival wrist resting positions. If an exact resting sample is missing, infer the resting endpoint from resting-site evidence at other visits in the currently visible demonstration together with the observed near-arrival trajectory. Do not use an already-departing wrist position as the preceding traversal's resting endpoint. At an intermediate x, wrist y smaller than the baseline y indicates the image-upper arc; wrist y larger than the baseline y indicates the image-lower arc. Use this lookup: increasing target x plus upper arc is A; decreasing target x plus lower arc is B; increasing target x plus lower arc is C; decreasing target x plus upper arc is D. Do not use target y, waypoint y, the attached-stick endpoint, or world height as the wrist baseline. Before serializing, audit the ledger: the number of letters must equal the number of adjacent-target arrival events, the first demonstrated traversal must still be present, and every letter must match its row's direction and independently classified arc under the four-case lookup. Repeated visits to the same pair may use different arcs; check each row's own evidence. Write one letter per traversal in chronological order, retaining repeated identical letters as separate commands. Write the full list at this first decision, without deleting the move selected now. The reset from the demonstration to the initial execution scene is not a completed oracle command and must not remove any letter. On a later decision with carried memory, the intervening execution shows the preceding oracle command completed at its adjacent target; remove exactly one leading letter from the carried list before selecting the next command. The decision-step protocol guarantees that each such return follows one completed command, so do not count individual frames or repeated highlights as additional completions. If there is no intervening completed execution, retain the carried list. Read the carried route as an ordered list serialized in a string. On every write, use square brackets and single-quoted uppercase menu letters, with exactly one space after each comma. Once exhausted, write the string []. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    First update remaining_path according to the policy prompt for memory. If its first letter is A, select A: move to the nearest robot-left target clockwise. If B, select B: move to the nearest robot-right target clockwise. If C, select C: move to the nearest robot-left target counterclockwise. If D, select D: move to the nearest robot-right target counterclockwise. These conditions apply regardless of the preceding subgoal: after any completed A, B, C, or D, transition to whichever letter now leads remaining_path. The current highlighted target is the departure site, not the destination. Robot-left selects the adjacent target with larger x and robot-right the adjacent target with smaller x; the menu handles these targets internally and requires no point. Initial subgoals decoded from the demonstrations are B for episode 0, A for episode 19, D for episode 58, A for episode 86, and A for episode 99. Never infer the next direction solely from the current location: identical locations can require different moves on repeated visits. If the list is empty, the demonstrated route is complete and no further traversal is intended. If an unexpected situation nevertheless requires a menu answer, or the demonstration cannot be decoded, choose A if a larger-x adjacent target exists, otherwise B if a smaller-x adjacent target exists, otherwise A; this is only a deterministic fallback, not an additional demonstrated move.

StopCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    passage_count
        Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, including the final decision observation after the preceding execution observations, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side (0 for empty memory). Compute the sign of cube x minus target x: strictly negative is -1 and strictly positive is 1, however small the separation. Do not introduce a proximity deadband or require a later confirmation frame. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. A change first visible in the final decision observation counts immediately. If the preceding side is 0, the first nonzero sign establishes the side without incrementing. At exact equality retain the working side and do not increment. Compute passage_count and last_side from this same scan and write both resulting values together. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
    last_side
        Write the working side resulting from the same chronological scan used for passage_count, after processing every newly shown observation including the final decision frame. Set it to -1 when cube x is strictly smaller than target x and 1 when it is strictly larger, even when the separation is small. Retain the preceding nonzero side only at exact equality; use 0 only if no nonzero side has yet been observed. Do not require a confirmation frame or wait for the cube to move clear of the target. Record this observed side, not the side expected after the selected command. e.g. -1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start in A: move to the top of the visible button to prepare. Select A whenever the hand is not yet in the prepared position. The prepared pose in these observations has the wrist above the button, height approximately 0.15, and closed fingers; do not mistake the wrist's image position for the fingertips' contact point. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. If passage_count equals N-1 and the next target passage is approximately 35 or fewer time units away, select C. Estimate the upcoming arrival from the chronological cube motion shown at this step, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. A useful estimate fits smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the current interval's timestamped cube positions and finds its next crossing of the visible target x; do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. In particular, an endpoint turnaround can already be the press-launch time for a fast cube. The final shown decisions in episodes 23 and 32 are such turnarounds; those in episodes 66, 94, and 99 show motion toward the requested next passage. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. If motion timing is uncertain, default to B while refining the estimate from the next observations, rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.
